items.title: Mantha, Kovacevic out at least one month for Devils
items.summary: Anthony Mantha and Johnathan Kovacevic will be out for an extended period, New Jersey Devils coach Sheldon Keefe said on Tuesday.
items.body: Forward sustained fractured throat, defenseman has high ankle sprain Anthony Mantha and Johnathan Kovacevic will be out for an extended period, New Jersey Devils coach Sheldon Keefe said on Tuesday. Mantha is projected to be out one month after the forward had surgery Monday to repair a fracture in his throat. He was injured in a 5-4 overtime win at the New York Islanders on Nov. 7 but should be able to resume skating in the near future. However, it’s uncertain when Mantha will be able to return. The Devils will need to evaluate when Mantha can safely withstand contact because of the unusual nature of the injury. "That one, I guess, from the way it's described to me, is going to be a tricky one because it's a very rare injury for any athlete, really," Keefe said. "So, it's just more so about when he'll be ready to take contact again, and they're going to feel that out." Kovacevic, a defenseman, is expected to miss 4-6 weeks because of a high ankle sprain he sustained in a 5-2 loss at the Winnipeg Jets on Nov. 10. He has two assists in 13 games and averages 14:40 of ice time. Brett Pesce (illness), however, was a full participant at practice Tuesday and is expected to return against the Montreal Canadiens at Prudential Center in Newark, New Jersey, on Wednesday (7:30 p.m. ET; MSGSN, Prime). The defenseman missed two games. Seamus Casey took another step in his recovery by skating on his own Tuesday. However, Keefe said he had not received an updated timetable for when the defenseman can play. Casey had knee surgery at the beginning of October after being injured during a preseason game at the New York Rangers on Sept. 24. The initial timeline for his recovery was 8-10 weeks.

items.title: Blues’ Adam Jecho cleared to return from NHL/NHLPA Player Assistance Program
items.summary: The St. Louis Blues announced Tuesday that forward Adam Jecho will report to their AHL affiliate, the Springfield Thunderbirds.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: (Steven Ellis/The Nation Network) The St. Louis Blues announced Tuesday that forward Adam Jecho has been cleared through the NHL/NHLPA Player Assistance Program and will rejoin the organization. The team said Jecho has been assigned to the Springfield Thunderbirds, their American Hockey League affiliate, and will report immediately. The league announced in September that Jecho would receive care from the player assistance program. A native of Zlin, Czechia, Jecho was taken No. 95 overall in the third round of the 2024 NHL Entry Draft. He signed a three-year, entry-level contract with the Blues that kicked in this season and will last through the 2028-29 campaign. The 6-foot-5 center spent three seasons with the Western Hockey League’s Edmonton Oil Kings, where he scored 58 goals and added 78 assists for 136 points in 157 career regular-season games. His best season came in 2024-25 where he recorded 25 goals and 28 assists for 53 points in 56 games. Going into Tuesday, the Blues are 9-9-2 with 20 points through their first 20 games of the 2026-27 regular season. They are seventh in the Central Division and three points back of the second Wildcard spot in the Western Conference. The Blues have a three-way tie for the team lead in points , with forwards Jimmy Snuggerud, Dylan Holloway and Robert Thomas all having 14 points. Snuggerud, 22, leads the team with 10 goals while Thomas leads with 11 assists. Philip Broberg leads all defenders with four goals and nine assists for 13 points and is averaging a team-high 24:33 of ice time per game.

The NHL/NHLPA release did not include why Jecho was receiving assistance from the program, which provides confidential support and treatment for players and their families dealing with mental health, substance use or other personal issues. He entered the program on Sept. 11. The 20-year-old centre from Zlin, Czechia, was selected in the third round, 95th overall, by the Blues in the 2024 NHL Draft. Jecho has yet to make his NHL debut and has spent the last three years with the WHL's Edmonton Oil Kings, where he totalled 136 points (58 goals, 78 assists) and 69 penalty minutes in 157 regular-season games. items.title: Stars’ Miro Heiskanen returns to lineup, Tyler Myers out with upper-body injury
items.summary: Heiskanen has missed the past five games due to an upper-body injury, and will give Dallas’ blue line a boost.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Kevin Jairaj-Imagn Images A big-time player is set to return to action in a marquee matchup. When speaking to the media, Dallas Stars head coach Glen Gulutzan stated that defenseman Miro Heiskanen will be in the lineup on Tuesday night, when the Stars take on the Vegas Golden Knights. He added that fellow rearguard Tyler Myers will miss the contest due to an upper-body injury. Heiskanen has missed the last five games due to an upper-body injury he suffered on Nov. 3, when he was hit hard against the boards by Washington Capitals defenseman Justin Sourdif. The Stars have managed to stay afloat during the Finnish defender’s absence, going 3-2-0 after a hard-fought overtime win over the Florida Panthers this past Sunday. In 15 games so far this year, Heiskanen has scored three goals and eight assists for 11 points, registering a plus/minus of +2 while averaging 24:53 of ice time per game. While the Gulutzan didn’t reveal any details, Myers was hurt during Sunday’s win over the Panthers. The 6-foot-8 d-man logged less than eight minutes of ice time during the contest. In 20 games thus far, Myers hasn’t found the back of the net, but has two assists to his name. He also has an even rating while averaging 16:20 of ice time. Myers’ injury only adds to the injuries suffered by the Stars’ blueliners this season. Along with Heiskanen, Lian Bichsel suffered a rough lower-body injury that is expected to keep him out for another week or so. The Stars (12-6-2) are fourth in the Central Division, eight points back of the first-place Minnesota Wild , and hold the first Wild Card spot in the Western Conference.

items.title: Sharks’ Kiefer Sherwood out week-to-week with upper-body injury
items.summary: Kiefer Sherwood has two goals and eight points in 23 games with the San Jose Sharks in 2026-27.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: David Gonzales The San Jose Sharks will be without one of their veteran forwards for the foreseeable future. Head coach Ryan Warsofsky told reporters Tuesday that Kiefer Sherwood will be out week-to-week with an upper-body injury, but that he doesn’t require surgery. Sherwood appeared to suffer the injury during the Sharks’ 4-2 win over the Nashville Predators Sunday. He finished the game with two shots and two hits in 10:55 of ice time. Sherwood, 31, has two goals and six assists for eight points in 23 games with the Sharks in 2026-27. He is in the first year of a five-year contract extension that carries a cap hit of $5.75 million through the 2030-31 season . Now in his ninth NHL season, the Columbus native has 68 goals and 74 assists for 142 points in 360 career regular-season games with the Sharks, Predators, Vancouver Canucks , Colorado Avalanche and Anaheim Ducks . His best offensive season came with the Canucks in 2024-25 where he scored 19 goals and added 21 assists for 40 points. Sherwood also has a goal and assist in eight playoff contests. The Sharks are 10-11-2 with 22 points through 23 games in 2026-27. They are fourth in the Pacific Division and one point back of the second Wildcard spot in the Western Conference. Captain Macklin Celebrini leads the team in all offensive categories with nine goals and 18 assists for 27 points. He also leads the team in ice time, averaging 23:07 per night. Meanwhile, defenseman Jacob Trouba is averaging 22:15 of ice time per game. Rookie forward Ivar Stenberg, the 2026 No. 2 overall pick, has seven goals and seven assists for 14 points in 23 games.

items.title: Vanguards sign Saskia Maurer to two-year contract
items.summary: The Swiss netminder was taken by the expansion team in the fourth round of the 2026 PWHL Draft.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: George Walker IV-USA TODAY Sports An underrated netminder is officially making the move to North America. On Tuesday, the Vegas Vanguards announced that the team has signed goaltender Saskia Maurer to a two-year contract, which will carry through the 2027-28 season. Maurer was taken by the Vanguards in the fourth round, 41st overall, of the 2026 PWHL Draft . She was the team’s fifth selection in the draft, and the fourth goaltender taken in Detroit . The Swiss netminder admitted she’s excited about the opportunity to play in the fast-growing league. “I’m really excited to join Las Vegas and be part of this team,” Maurer said in a release. “It’s a great new challenge, and I’m looking forward to getting started and seeing where this journey takes us.” Maurer has made a name for herself on the international stage. She has been part of Switzerland’s senior national team since the 2019 IIHF Women’s World Championship, backing up Andrea Brandli for the past few years. She also represented her country at the Winter Olympics in 2022 and 2026, really helping Switzerland play well in the group stage with Brandli missing the first couple of games due to Norovirus this past February. In Milan, Maurer went 1-2-0, with a 3.25 goals-against average and a .918 save percentage, helping Switzerland win its first Olympic bronze medal in 12 years. Maurer held a similar role during the 2026 IIHF Women’s World Championship. With a 1-2-0 record again, she also had a 1.67 GAA and a .944 SV%. Unfortunately, she was on the wrong end of a 1-0 quarterfinal loss to Sweden last Friday. items.summary: The organization’s website had a rather ominous post about teams not wanting to play Russia.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: John E. Sokolowski-USA TODAY Sports It looks like some people are trying to take action against the International Ice Hockey Federation for their recent decisions. On Tuesday, the IIHF website was the victim of a cyberattack. The attack came from pro-Russian supporters who clearly aren’t fans of the recent announcement that Russia will not be participating in the 2027 IIHF World Junior Championship. The headline image read, “Scared to face Russia?” With a subheader stating, “You banned the only team you can’t beat.” In a statement , the IIHF confirmed that the site was hacked and that it is making the right decisions during what has been a trying time for the game. “We strongly condemn these actions and are taking all necessary steps to investigate the source of the attack and restore our systems,” the statement said. “Our platforms will be back online as soon as we are confident they are secure. The IIHF remains committed to protecting the integrity of our organization and safeguarding our sport.” There has been no confirmation of who or what orchestrated the cyberattack. As of 2 p.m. ET, IIHF.com is still down. items.title: Flames’ Huberdeau seeks more answers as he returns to action
items.summary: The toughest part of Jonathan Huberdeau’s hip resurfacing recovery wasn’t the pain, the gruelling rehabilitation or even the first three months he spent unable to skate. It was the uncertainty.
items.body: CALGARY — The toughest part of Jonathan Huberdeau ’s hip resurfacing recovery wasn’t the pain, the gruelling rehabilitation or even the first three months he spent unable to skate. Would he play again? Would the pain return? Would he ever be the same player? And, perhaps most importantly, would he be able to enjoy a normal life without constantly wondering what his hip had in store for him? “I think it's just ups and downs,” Huberdeau said, describing the mental gymnastics of an eight-month rehabilitation following surgery. “Are you gonna come back, or are you gonna be as good as before? Better than before? Not as good? There was some point that I was hurting a lot, and you're like, ‘OK, well, is it gonna be like this for the rest of my life?” Devin Cooley, the Flames' resident philosopher, certainly has a gift for putting things in perspective. Whatever the secret, Huberdeau is finally ready to put the uncertainty behind him and get back to playing hockey. The 33-year-old Flames winger will make his long-awaited return to game action Wednesday night at the Saddledome when he suits up for the Calgary Wranglers on an injury conditioning loan that represents the biggest milestone yet in his comeback from surgery last March. Eight months after going under the knife, he's nervous, excited and understandably eager to find out what happens when the puck drops. “I mean, I haven't played for a while. I think that's just a normal part. But I just gotta take it and embrace it.” The date has been a moving target since he shut things down last February, with Huberdeau wisely resisting the temptation to put a firm timetable on a procedure so uncommon among hockey players that there isn't much of a playbook. items.title: Which teams have underwhelmed so far this season?

items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Daniel Kucin Jr. We’re at the quarter-mark of the 2026-27 NHL regular season, and while some teams are right where fans and pundits expected them to be, others have looked underwhelming through their first 20-plus games. On Tuesday’s episode of Daily Faceoff LIVE , Tyler Yaremchuk and former NHL goaltender Carter Hutton share which teams they believe have underperformed so far this season and what they need to get their seasons back on track. Tyler Yaremchuk : I was thinking the Carolina Hurricanes might have a tinge of a Stanley Cup hangover, but I thought the Washington Capitals , with everything they did in the offseason, all the signing and spending, the thought was they would be right there with the Hurricanes. Instead, they’re right there with the New York Rangers, the New York Islanders and all those other teams in the mush of the Eastern Conference . A big reason for that is a bit of a step back from Logan Thompson. Last year, he was fourth among qualified goalies in goals saved above expected, but so far this season, he’s 24th in the league. This is a team that’s giving up the sixth-highest expected goals at five-on-five. Defensively, they haven’t been what they’ve been in the past, and Thompson has sputtered a little bit to start the season. items.body: Down 4-0 to the Montreal Canadiens and less than three minutes from their 10th consecutive loss, Winnipeg engineered a never-before-seen comeback . That Nov. 3 win has galvanized the Jets, who have won six in a row, including erasing another four-goal deficit Saturday against the Chicago Blackhawks. (Winnipeg became the second team in NHL history with multiple four-goal comeback wins over a six-game span.) “To see the character in this room that there’s no giving up, there’s always fight and especially at a time when we lost a bunch in a row and it’s really easy to lay your gloves down and be done and move on to the next one, to see the team keep fighting and get that win (against the Canadiens), it’s almost impossible not to get a spark out of that,” Jets centre and new franchise points leader Mark Scheifele told reporters . Under the terms of the CBA, a player who has been out with a long-term injury, defined as missing at least 24 days and 10 games, can be sent to the AHL on a conditioning loan. While he is with the Wranglers, Huberdeau won’t count towards Calgary’s active NHL roster, but will count towards the NHL salary cap. The 33-year-old Huberdeau underwent hip surgery in the spring and has not played a competitive game since Feb. 4, when he scored in a 4-3 Flames win over the Edmonton Oilers . Before his injury, he posted 10 goals and 15 assists in 50 games with the Flames, bringing his NHL career totals to 263 goals, 544 assists and 807 points in 962 games since making his debut with the Florida Panthers in the 2012-13 season. “I’m feeling pretty good. It’s a big surgery,” Huberdeau said in September. “There’s no pain anymore, which is nice to deal with. Just now, the goal is to come back and be 100%.” Now with the Wranglers, he could return at home on Tuesday and Wednesday night against the Coachella Valley Firebirds, before the team heads on the road to take on the Laval Rocket on Saturday and Sunday. If his recovery and form-building remain on track, he could be with the Flames as soon as next week, as they enjoy a mediocre start to the 2026-27 season, with 19 points in their first 21 games and four short of the final Wild Card spot in the Western Conference.

The statue is expected to be unveiled in the spring of 2028. The bronze sculpture, designed by New Jersey-based artist Carl LeVotch, will stand five-foot-nine. LeVotch is aiming for the statue to recognize the "humility, kindness, family devotion, perseverance and sportsmanship" that defined the Gaudreaus' lives. LeVotch is working with the Gaudreau Brothers Sculpture Project, a non-profit organization, to help fund the design. Mandatory Credit: Dan Hamilton-Imagn Images What do you want the goalie on your favorite NHL team to be thinking while he protects a lead in the final seconds of a game? It’s tough to imagine a more inspiring mantra than what Devon Levi uttered to himself with 10 seconds left on the clock Saturday night and superstar Auston Matthews poised to fire a backhander from the slot. Levi didn’t flinch or quake or shrink in his crease as he stared down the Toronto Maple Leafs captain. Levi met the challenge with a smile and battled through a flurry of desperate chances as his Edmonton Oilers held on for a 1-0 road win at Scotiabank Arena. It marked the first shutout of Levi’s NHL career, and it improved his record to 9-1-0 in what has been a stellar start to his 2026-27 season. After the game, Levi, 24, beamed with pride as he spoke to reporters and recounted his inner monologue during that climactic scramble. He wore the expression of a young man whose dreams were coming true but also someone who appreciates how unlikely the moment seemed even half a year earlier. As recently as last season, Levi existed in a purgatory somewhere between a prospect sure to become an impactful NHLer and “It would’ve happened by now.” Acquired as the centerpiece to the Buffalo Sabres’ trade of Sam Reinhart to the Florida Panthers in 2021, Levi was considered a borderline can’t-miss star in his late teens to early 20s. items.title: Canucks Takeaways: Tolopilo’s stellar outing fuels second straight win
items.summary: Nikita Tolopilo had a brilliant 34-save performance on Monday as the Canucks beat the Mammoth for their first winning streak of the season.
items.body: If the plan was to reward third-string goalie Nikita Tolopilo for his fine minor-league play by giving him a National Hockey League start on a back-to-back and then sending him back to the American League, the Vancouver Canucks should rethink things. Of course, we don’t know what the plan is — or was — because NHL teams at the bottom of the standings do not ordinarily clutter their active roster with a third goalie, but Tolopilo’s first game for the Canucks since last season should earn him a longer stay. The 26-year-old goalie, who cleared NHL waivers in September on his way back to the minors, had a brilliant 34-save performance Monday in Salt Lake City as the Canucks beat the Utah Mammoth 3-2 for Vancouver’s first winning streak of the season. After losing 17 of their previous 18 games to pass the quarter mark of their schedule with one of the worst records in NHL history, the Canucks swept the Mammoth and Vegas Golden Knights in just over 24 hours for their first consecutive wins. Stanley Cup contenders, the Knights are a heavy, physical team. The Mammoth are pretty heavy, too, but with considerably more speed and youth. And the Canucks beat them by an aggregate score of 9-5 to re-energize themselves after a bleak, dispiriting start to their rebuild season. Starting goalie Leevi Merilainen was the best Canuck in Vegas, and Tolopilo was even better in Utah. It seemed like a peculiar decision to recall Tolopilo on Sunday to give Merilainen a breather in the back-to-back because Vancouver is stuck with struggling veteran Kevin Lankinen and his no-move-clause contract. But Tolopilo made general manager Ryan Johnson look like a genius as the Canucks were outshot 36-24, including 21-8 over the first 34 minutes. items.title: Boeser’s late power-play goal lifts Canucks to win over Mammoth
items.summary: Brock Boeser scored a power-play goal with 4:23 left to lift the Vancouver Canucks to a 3-2 victory over the Utah Mammoth on Monday night.
items.body: SALT LAKE CITY — Brock Boeser scored a power-play goal with 4:23 left to lift the Vancouver Canucks to a 3-2 victory over the Utah Mammoth on Monday night. Jake DeBrusk flicked the puck out to Boeser and he threaded it inside the post to help Vancouver win consecutive games for the first time this season. DeBrusk and Filip Chytil also scored goals for the Canucks. Nikita Tolopilo made 32 saves in his season debut for Vancouver. Vincent Trocheck and Barrett Hayton scored for Utah, which lost is sixth straight game. Karel Vejmelka had 21 stops for the Mammoth. Neither team found the net until DeBrusk chipped in a power-play goal at the post with 4:55 left in the second. Vancouver scored 10 seconds into the power play after Boeser crossed the puck into DeBrusk while he battled Lawson Crouse for position at the post. Trocheck got Utah on the board at 2:51 of the third, snapping in the puck on a power play. The Canucks regained the lead on Chytil’s goal at 4:40 of the third. Chytil drew Vejmelka out to the post, wrapped around the net, and deflected the puck off the goaltender’s heel for the easy goal. Hayton leveled the score again with 8:20 left, snapping the puck over Tolopilo’s shoulder.

items.title: Struggling power play deflates Canadiens in loss to Rangers
items.summary: The sooner the Canadiens can sort out their power play, the better. The unit’s struggles hadn’t been particularly costly up to this point, but an 0-for-4 showing deflated Montreal in Monday’s loss to the Rangers.
items.body: NEW YORK — Any time you give up a goal on your own power play before even registering a shot on net, you know it’s going to be a bad night. It was arguably their worst one since they started their season with a fortunate 3-2 win in Toronto on Sept. 29. That victory over the Maple Leafs was one of two nights in which the Canadiens had all their power-play regulars available to them, which is undeniably part of the reason why their power play has been dysfunctional for the last 19 games. But even without Ivan Demidov—a dynamic, triple-threat player who can shoot, pass and deke opponents to open up all kinds of options—it shouldn’t be this bad. “Demi’s a special player and a threat when he has it, when he’s shooting it,” said Nick Suzuki . “Obviously we miss him, but I feel like we have the talent and the players to make up for that.” Suzuki is one of them, though his six-game absence didn’t help the power play. Cole Caufield , who’s coming off a 51-goal season, has been there all along, and he’s an elite power-play option. As is Juraj Slafkovsky, who scored 15 of his career-high 30 goals last season on the man advantage. And if Lane Hutson isn’t the best power-play quarterback in the league, he isn’t far off. But even with all of them in place and sniper Zachary Bolduc in Demidov’s spot, the Canadiens’ top unit hasn’t clicked. And it takes up too much time for the second unit to pick up the slack. items.title: Canadiens give up three unanswered goals in loss to Rangers
items.body: NEW YORK — Will Cuylle scored twice, including the go-ahead short-handed goal in the final minute of the second period, and the New York Rangers rallied to defeat the Montreal Canadiens 3-1 on Monday night. The Rangers have won three in a row and six of their past seven and improved to 9-2-0 at home. Their latest victory followed a ceremony commemorating the 100th anniversary of the first game in franchise history, which came against the Montreal Maroons. Once the puck dropped, the Canadiens dominated for stretches with the puck in the offensive zone. That allowed them to take the lead when Lane Hutson spun around Matt Rempe and put a shot in the perfect place for Phillip Danault to deflect it into the net. Their advantage lasted less than two minutes. With Juraj Slafkovský slow to guard Marcus Pettersson back down the ice, the defenseman banked the puck off Cuylle in the crease to bring life to a fired-up crowd inside Madison Square Garden. Montreal then showed why it ranks second to last in the NHL on the power play despite overflowing with talent from Hutson and Slafkovský to Cole Caufield and Nick Suzuki. When the top unit failed to score, Alex Newhook missing the net paved the way for Cuylle to get a head of steam and beat Jacob Fowler short side off the rush with 56.3 seconds left in the second. Another unsuccessful Canadiens power play in the third was cut short by an interference penalty on Noah Dobson. Scott Morrow scored just his second career goal with 13:16 left. Fowler allowed three goals on 26 shots. At the other end, Joonas Korpisalo made 24 saves to win for the third time in as many starts since missing the first five-plus weeks of the season because of injury. The Golden Knights traded defenseman Jeremy Davies to the Wild, and the Wild sent forward Gerald Mayhew to the Golden Knights organization. The Ste-Anne-de-Bellevue, QC, native was originally drafted by the New Jersey Devils with the 192nd overall pick (seventh round) in the 2016 NHL Draft. Davies eventually signed a two-year, entry-level contract with the Devils, but was traded to the Nashville Predators a few months later in the P.K. Subban trade. Beginning his professional career shortly before the COVID-19 pandemic, Davies never gathered any momentum with Nashville, or anywhere else, for that matter. Now into his eighth professional campaign, Davies has blossomed into a solid AHL defenseman with very little NHL experience. items.body: Winnipeg Jets centre Mark Scheifele , Minnesota Wild goaltender Jesper Wallstedt and Carolina Hurricanes left-wing Nikolaj Ehlers have been named the NHL's three stars of the week. Scheifele led the league with three goals and five assists in three games as the Jets extended their winning streak to six contests. The 33-year-old Scheifele now has 933 points (379 goals, 554 assists), surpassing the old franchise record of 929 set by Dale Hawerchuk in 1990. He also moved past Thomas Steen for the franchise assists record and tied Hawerchuk for the Jets' goals mark. Wallstedt went 3-0-0 with a 1.66 goals-against average and .944 save percentage to backstop the Central Division-leading Wild to a perfect three-game road trip. The 24-year-old tops the NHL with 14 wins through 19 appearances this season and is 8-0-1 in his last nine starts dating to Oct. 24. items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Charles LeClaire-USA TODAY Sports Maybe Father Time has finally forced one of the greatest players of all time to call it a day. If you have nothing more to give and you feel like you’re doing more harm than good, it’s time to leave. But I think I’ve squeezed every last drop out of it.” Jagr last played in the NHL nine years ago, putting an end to one of the greatest careers in NHL history. items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Rob Gray-Imagn Images Amid a terrible two months to start the 2026-27 season, the Toronto Maple Leafs ‘ brass seems to be sticking with the process. When speaking to the media on Monday, Maple Leafs general manager John Chayka publicly gave a vote of confidence to head coach Jim Hiller. “We got a lot of confidence in Jim,” Chayka said. “Mats and I have our full support behind him. And I think adversity is an opportunity to learn, an opportunity to grow. I think you have really have to be honest where you’re at, what you’ve done, what needs to improve.” It has been a rocky start to the Jim Hiller era in Toronto. The man who Chayka hired has done little to help the team improve after missing out on the Stanley Cup Playoffs last season. As of Monday, the team is on a six-game losing streak, losing eight of their past nine. Toronto lost each matchup in its recent four-game homestand, capped off with a 1-0 loss to the Edmonton Oilers on Saturday night. The consistent failure of the Leafs through the first quarter of the new season is having fans call for an immediate change behind the bench. When chatting with reporters, Chayka added that “fans deserve better,” something he said a couple of times. Yet, no changes seem to be coming from the Original Six franchise at this time. items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Amber Searls-Imagn Images The drought is over. Thanks to Ebba Svensson Traff’s heroics in the shootout, Sweden defeated Finland to win the bronze medal at the 2026 IIHF Women’s World Championship. It is Sweden’s first medal at the Women’s Worlds since 2007, and the program’s third bronze medal overall. Finland came short of winning a record 16th bronze at the WWC. In another thrilling battle between the Scandinavian rivals. Back and forth, the two teams traded chances, but neither could find the back of the net until Michelle Karvinen tipped in an Elisa Holopainen point shot on the power play for her second of the tournament, putting the Finns out in front. Sweden managed to use the player advantage to level the game in the waning minutes of regulation, as Lina Ljungblom finished off a nice feed from Hanna Thuvik for her second of the tournament. After neither team scored for the remainder of regulation, overtime was required. However, both Svensson Traff and Sanni Ahola made some big saves in the extra frame. In the skills competition, Tilde Grillfors and Hilda Svensson both scored for the Swedes, while Noora Tulus was the only one to find the back of the net for Finland, through Karvinen rang one off the crossbar. Sweden outshot Finland 37-30 in the contest. Along with her three saves in the shootout, Svensson Traff turned away 29 shots in the victorious effort. Ahola made 35 stops in the loss. It was a little bit of redemption for Sweden, a team that lost to Switzerland in an exciting bronze medal clash at the 2026 Winter Olympics. items.summary: Martin St. Louis was steadfast in his belief that the Canadiens should embrace their contender status, not waste time debating it. So far there hasn’t been much of a debate, Eric Engels writes in his quarter-mark report card.
items.body: NEW YORK — When we sat down with Montreal Canadiens coach Martin St. Louis before the season got underway, he talked about how his team should embrace its contender status and waste no time debating whether it’s been earned. “I think the biggest thing for our group to understand is this is where we are,” St. Louis said. “We won two playoff rounds; let’s accept this is where we are. We have to understand how we got here, because it wasn’t luck. Luck has nothing to do with why we’re here. Are we on time? Are we ahead? Who cares, this is where we are. When you accept where you are, now there’s more responsibilities. We had to accept where we were two years ago and get to work. items.body: The Vancouver Canucks ' long, dark autumn of despair began with a loss against the Vegas Golden Knights. They hope Sunday’s surprising 6-3 win in Las Vegas will be the end of it. With one of their best and most complete performances in what has been a historically bad season so far, the Canucks got goals from throughout their lineup, a 34-save performance from goalie Leevi Merilainen and timely responses whenever the Golden Knights pressed them. It was proof of what Vancouver coach Manny Malhotra has been preaching: that when the Canucks play a simple, direct game and play it for three periods, the National Hockey League’s last-place team can be competitive. items.summary: With two assists on Sunday, McDavid has 41 assists through 22 games this season.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Connor McDavid has been making hockey look far too easy so far in the 2026-27 NHL season, and the Edmonton Oilers star center just earned yet another eye-popping accomplishment. During the Oilers’ 5-2 win over the Philadelphia Flyers on Sunday, McDavid notched a goal and two assists, giving him 41 assists through 22 games played this season. That ties Wayne Gretzky’s mark from the 1984-85 season for the fewest games to reach 40 assists to start a season. McDavid, 29, had already become the fastest player in NHL history to reach 30 assists this season, when he had an assist in a 4-1 win over the New York Rangers on November 1 to accomplish the feat in 15 games. By getting on the score sheet on Sunday, McDavid also extended his career-best point streak to 22 games. The Oilers’ captain has always been a dominant offensive force, but he’s been scoring at an especially ridiculous rate this season. With his three points against the Flyers, McDavid has 12 goals and 41 assists for 53 points in 22 games. That puts him on pace for a 200-point season, which is something that has only ever been achieved by Gretzky, who did so four times for Edmonton in the 1980s. Even if McDavid cools off a bit from his current torrid pace, he still stands a very strong chance to have the best scoring season of his career. His most productive season to date came in 2022-23, when he registered 64 goals and 89 assists for 153 points in all 82 games. The three-time Hart Trophy winner has led Edmonton to 35 points through 22 games, good for first place in the Pacific Division . The Oilers will continue their current six-game road trip when they visit the Florida Panthers on Tuesday.

items.title: Devin Cooley sees goaltending — and life — differently. Other pro goalies are starting to take notice.
items.summary: Cooley's viral interviews have sparked a larger conversation about pressure, perspective, and the mental demands of professional goaltending.
items.body: Cooley’s philosophical postgame quotes have captivated hockey fans, from his mantra of “Nothing matters. Nobody cares. We’re all going to die,” to the existential insight of “The past is dead. There’s nothing for you there.” Fans aren’t the only ones paying attention. Cooley’s fellow NHL goalies have been watching along as he delivers answers fresh off a motivational poster, offering an alternative to the bland quotes players are used to giving. “A lot of answers you see in a hockey locker room are pretty freaking boring and cliche,” Capitals goaltender Charlie Lindgren told RMNB. “There’s not much to it, it’s kind of the same old answers. Now he steps into the fold and completely different. “He’s obviously a very unique human being. I don’t know him personally, but you can just tell, the way he’s thinking and talking, he’s definitely more of a deep thinker, and he’s not going to give you the standard answers. He’s going to go out and be himself and answer the questions the way he wants to.” View this post on Instagram Becoming an “unconscious goalie” Cooley’s approach to goaltending, in particular, has struck a chord with his peers. He’s repeatedly emphasized the importance of, in effect, turning his brain off when he’s in net to let his instincts do the work. “The problem with me is that I have a lot of fun playing, but when I start having too much fun, it [changes me] from an unconscious goalie to a conscious goalie,” he told Sportsnet’s Brendan Parker last month. “And my conscious brain is really bad at playing goalie. So I have to let my unconscious brain do the work, because it reacts a lot quicker…Like, don’t think about anything. items.title: Oilers’ McDavid ties Gretzky’s record for fewest games to record 40 assists
items.summary: Connor McDavid is showing shades of Wayne Gretzky once again.
items.body: Connor McDavid is showing shades of Wayne Gretzky once again. The Edmonton Oilers captain tied Gretzky's record for the fewest games to record 40 assists, doing so in his 22nd contest of the season against the Philadelphia Flyers on Sunday. McDavid took a pass from Leon Draisaitl in the slot and fed a backhand pass right back to his linemate for a one-timer power-play goal. It came one day after McDavid extended his point streak to a career-best 21 games and reached 50 points on the season with an assist to Evan Bouchard against the Maple Leafs on Saturday. However, the 29-year-old superstar is still far from that record. Gretzky holds the NHL record for the longest point streak at 51 games, which he set in the 1983-84 season with the Oilers. Gretzky piled up a ridiculous 61 goals and 92 assists over the 51-game streak, and went on to finish the season with 205 points. McDavid, now at 11 goals and 41 assists over his 22-game tear, is on pace for 199 points this season. Only Gretzky has ever surpassed the 200-point mark, a feat he accomplished four times over his career.

items.body: Register Login Lineup Notes: Heiskanen, Sharks, Gudas By Bradley Keith | at November 15, 2026 8:03 pm Dallas hopes Miro Heiskanen can return Tuesday in Vegas, Stars reporter and NHL.com correspondent Robert Tiffin reports . The elite defender hasn’t played since his upper-body injury sustained on November 3 against Washington, taking a hard hit from Justin Sourdif . Impressively, missing their #1 defenseman for the last four games, Dallas has picked up five out of a possible eight points including a shutout win over Buffalo yesterday. Speaking to the strength on their blueline, they’ve been in good hands leaning on the trio of Thomas Harley , Esa Lindell , and Nils Lundqvist . So far this season Lundqvist’s usage has surpassed the 18-minute mark, the highest of his career. Harley has also enjoyed a noticeable uptick, currently leading the team in average ice time at over 25 minutes a game. Prior to going down, the 27-year-old Heiskanen looked like his normal elite self with 11 points in 15 games, still ranked 13th in the league with his 24:53 of usage per game. Dealing with a major knee injury in the past, the Finn has mostly been durable, although he hasn’t gotten through a campaign without missing a single game since being a rookie eight years ago. Having to play without him again tonight against Florida, Dallas hopes he’ll be all set against the Golden Knights in the week ahead.

items.body: Register Login Evening Notes: Wright, Canadiens, Blues By Bradley Keith | at November 15, 2026 6:01 pm Former Kraken forward Shane Wright never formally asked out of Seattle or demanded a trade, he said in an interview with Andrew Knoll of RG.org . Drafted fourth overall in 2022 to be a significant building block in their early days as a franchise, Wright never put it all together for the Kraken and was traded two weeks ago to Nashville for Matthew Wood . It was first reported back in July that the two sides were headed for a split. Wright’s agent Kurt Overhardt had said then that GM Jason Botterill “agreed to move Shane this summer” although it took until November while the center continued to tread water with four points in his last 14 games wearing the Kraken uniform. Finally finding the right return, Seattle brought in Nashville’s 15th overall selection three years ago in Wood, who was former GM Barry Trotz ’s first pick in his new role. The 21-year-old scored 17 goals in his first full NHL campaign, but he was off to a slow start with just one tally in his first 14 this fall. items.body: Anderson, Matheson to miss time for Canadiens; Panarin away from Kings after grandfather dies Welcome to the NHL Status Report. Here is the latest lineup/injury news around the NHL. Miro Heiskanen missed his fifth straight game for the Stars with an upper-body injury, a 2-1 overtime win against the Florida Panthers on Sunday. The defenseman left early in the second period of a 6-5 win at the Washington Capitals on Nov. 3 after he was hit into the boards by Justin Sourdif . The Stars hope to get him back this week when they play two road games at the Vegas Golden Knights on Tuesday and Thursday. "We'll just have to see how he is," coach Glen Gulutzan said. "If it's not the first game, I would think probably the odds go up even more that it's the second game, but hopefully it's the first. But we'll see how he's doing." items.title: Rangers Move Igor Shesterkin To Season-Ending LTIR
items.summary: The New York Rangers have moved goaltender Igor Shesterkin to season-ending LTIR.
items.body: Register Login Rangers Move Igor Shesterkin To Season-Ending LTIR By Brian La Rose | at November 15, 2026 5:00 pm The Rangers have quietly made a move to open up considerably more salary cap flexibility. PuckPedia reports ( Twitter link ) that the Rangers have transferred goaltender Igor Shesterkin from regular LTIR to season-ending LTIR. The placement means that the netminder won’t be able to return at any point in 2026-27, either in the regular season or the playoffs. Considering he was ruled out for the season when he sustained a leg injury last month, the Rangers aren’t really taking any sort of risk making this move. When a player goes on regular LTIR, the cap flexibility created is capped at the lower of the player’s AAV or last year’s average salary, roughly $3.9MM this season. That amount is also reduced by the amount of regular cap space the team has at the time. This is the route New York initially took, giving them ample flexibility to recall Dylan Garand at the time of the injury and make other needed roster moves as well. However, when a player is moved to season-ending LTIR, the player’s full cap hit becomes spendable again, minus any existing cap room or existing LTIR usage. That’s especially notable when you consider that Shesterkin has the highest cap hit for a goalie in NHL history, checking in at $11,567,857. Per PuckPedia , the Rangers now have roughly $9MM in LTIR room at their disposal after today’s acquisition of Arvid Soderblom . They technically didn’t need to make this move to facilitate the trade as they had nearly $3MM in regular LTIR room beforehand and Soderblom only cut down about half of that.
